The Science

What Is Ceramic Coating?

Ceramic coating is a liquid polymer applied by hand to a vehicle's exterior. It chemically bonds to the factory paint, forming a second skin of protection that cannot be washed or wiped away.

The key ingredient is Silicon Dioxide (SiO₂) — the same material in quartz and glass — suspended in a carrier liquid. Once cured, it creates an ultra-hard, hydrophobic layer rated at up to 9H on the pencil hardness scale (harder than your car's clear coat).

Unlike wax that sits on top of the paint and degrades in weeks, or sealants that last a few months, professional ceramic coating permanently bonds to the clear coat and lasts for years with proper maintenance.

Why Ceramic

What It Does for Your Car

Ceramic coating doesn't just make your car look better — it fundamentally changes how your paint interacts with the world around it.

💧
Extreme Hydrophobicity
Water beads up and rolls off the surface completely, carrying dirt and contaminants with it. Rain essentially self-cleans your car on the highway.
☀️
UV & Oxidation Shield
Ceramic deflects UV rays that cause paint to fade, oxidize, and chalk over time. Your color stays richer and deeper for years longer.
🪨
Chemical Resistance
Bird droppings, tree sap, acid rain, and road chemicals can etch unprotected clear coat in hours. Ceramic coating resists all of them.
✨
Permanent High Gloss
The coating adds depth and a glass-like reflectivity to the paint. That showroom-wet look doesn't fade — it's locked in for the life of the coating.
🧹
Easier to Keep Clean
Dirt and grime have nothing to grip. Maintenance washes take a fraction of the time, and the car stays cleaner between washes naturally.
🛡️
Scratch Resistance
At 9H hardness, the coating absorbs minor surface contact that would scratch unprotected paint — protecting your investment against everyday wear.
Know the Difference

Ceramic vs. Sealant vs. Wax

Not all paint protection is equal. Here's how professional ceramic coating stacks up against our 6-month ceramic sealant (included in the Platinum Detail) and a traditional carnauba wax.

Feature Ceramic Coating 6-Mo Ceramic Sealant
(Platinum Detail)		 Carnauba Wax
Protection Duration 2–5 Years 4–6 Months 4–8 Weeks
Bonding Method Chemical bond to clear coat Semi-permanent adhesion Sits on surface, no bond
Hydrophobic Effect Extreme (100°+ contact angle) Good (moderate beading) Minimal
UV Protection Full UV deflection Partial Very limited
Chemical Resistance High — resists etching Moderate Low
Scratch Resistance 9H hardness rating Minor surface protection None
Gloss Enhancement Deep, permanent glass gloss Good temporary shine Warm glow, fades quickly
Application Time Full day service Included in detail 30–60 minutes
Cost Over 5 Years One-time investment Reapplied each detail Repeated every 4–8 weeks
Best For Long-term protection & max value Maintaining between coatings Quick cosmetic touch-up

Our take: The 6-month ceramic sealant in our Platinum Detail is genuinely excellent — and for clients getting regular details, it provides continuous protection when reapplied every visit. But if you want set-it-and-forget-it protection that lasts years, professional ceramic coating is in a different league entirely. Both products have a place; the right choice depends on your goals.

Our Method

The Coating Process

Ceramic coating is only as good as the surface it's applied to. We never skip steps — rushed prep is the most common reason coatings fail early.

01
Paint Correction
All defects are removed first. Coating over swirls or scratches locks them in permanently. This is the most critical and time-intensive step.
02
Full Decontamination
Iron remover, clay bar, and panel wipe-down eliminate every trace of contamination. Any residue under the coating will cause bonding failure.
03
Coating Application
Applied panel by panel by hand using a specialized applicator block. Even, overlapping passes ensure full, uniform coverage with no missed spots.
04
Leveling & Cure
Each panel is buffed to remove high spots and ensure a flawless, gloss finish. The coating then cures over 24–48 hours to reach full hardness.

Before You Coat

Start with Paint Correction

Ceramic coating is permanent — it seals whatever is underneath it. Apply it over swirl marks or scratches, and those defects are locked in for the life of the coating.

For that reason, we strongly recommend pairing ceramic coating with paint correction — especially for vehicles with visible swirling, scratches, or oxidation. That said, many newer vehicles or well-maintained cars have paint in excellent condition and can go straight to coating without any correction needed. We'll assess your paint honestly and tell you exactly what we recommend before any work begins.

When you do combine the two services, the result is paint that's both optically flawless and permanently protected — the full Drew's Precision experience.

Common Questions

FAQ

Everything you need to know before committing to ceramic coating.

How long does ceramic coating last?
Depending on the package, our coatings last 1, 3, or 5 years. Longevity depends on how the vehicle is maintained — hand washing vs. automatic car washes, where it's stored, and environmental exposure. Avoiding automated brush car washes dramatically extends coating life.
Does ceramic coating prevent all scratches?
No coating is truly scratch-proof. At 9H hardness, ceramic coating is significantly harder than your clear coat and resists minor surface contact and swirl marks from washing. Deep key scratches or rock chips will still cause damage — for those, PPF (paint protection film) is the right solution.
Can it be applied over my existing wax or sealant?
No. All existing wax, sealant, and contamination must be fully removed before application. Any residue left on the surface prevents the ceramic from bonding correctly and will cause it to fail prematurely. Our decontamination process ensures a perfectly clean substrate.
How long until I can drive my car after coating?
We recommend avoiding washing and extended water exposure for 48–72 hours after application to allow full initial cure. You can drive after roughly 12 hours, but treat it gently. Full hardness is reached at approximately 3 weeks.
Do I still need to wash my car after coating?
Yes — ceramic coating makes washing easier and less frequent, but it doesn't eliminate the need for washing. A proper hand wash every 2–4 weeks is still recommended. The difference is that dirt barely bonds to the surface and comes off much more easily.
How much does ceramic coating cost?
Pricing is based on vehicle size, paint condition, and the package selected. We provide transparent quotes after an in-person assessment — no surprises. Contact us to schedule a free consultation and we'll walk you through the right option for your vehicle and budget.
